brief.userPrompt: A malicious actor manipulates the AODB so FIDS, BHS and PA mislead passengers; test data integrity, public trust and crowd management.
learningObjectives: Coordinate public messaging across IT, Ops, and PIO during a reputational crisis
Make high-consequence operational decisions on incomplete or conflicting technical data
Identify the root cause using provided logs

overview.theme: Data Integrity, Public Trust, and Crowd Management.
overview.threat: A malicious actor has gained access to the airport's "Airport Operational Database" (AODB), which feeds data to the Flight Information Display Systems (FIDS), Baggage Handling System (BHS), and the automated Public Address (PA) system.
overview.operationalImpact: Passengers are misinformed, directed to the wrong gates, or told their flights are cancelled when they aren't. This causes crowding, missed flights, and potential safety hazards.

overview.targetAudience: Airport Operations, IT/Cybersecurity, Public Safety, Public Information (PIO).

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to coordinate public messaging across IT, Ops, and PIO functions during a reputational crisis.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to make high-consequence operational decisions (e.g., "Go Dark") based on incomplete or conflicting technical data.

objectives.name: Technical Analysis
objectives.text: Correctly identify the root cause (SQL Injection / Compromised Credential) using provided logs.

roles.name: Ops Director
roles.description: Incident Commander. Manages the physical terminal and passenger safety.

roles.name: IT Director
roles.description: Technical Lead. Manages the investigation and system restoration.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Manages social media and press inquiries.

roles.name: Airport Security Coordinator
roles.description: Monitors crowd temper and physical security.

roles.name: Airline Liaison
roles.description: Represents the frustration of the tenant airlines (Skyline, HWK Air, etc.).

phases.title: The Glitch
phases.goal: To test initial problem identification and the reluctance to declare an incident.

phases.title: The Crisis
phases.goal: To escalate the situation to a point where "Business as Usual" is impossible.

phases.title: Manual Mode
phases.goal: To force the transition from digital tools to analog/manual procedures.

phases.title: Recovery & Verification
phases.goal: To manage the complex process of "trusting the data" again.

msel.event: STARTEX (Start Exercise). Current time: 09:00 AM on a busy Thursday. Weather is clear. Passenger load is high due to a holiday weekend.
msel.expectedAction: Establish baseline operations. Review TIRP Section 13.

citations.documentTitle: Terminal Incident Response Plan

msel.event: Phone Call: "Hey Ops, this is Skyline at Gate B4. The screen above the gate says this flight is going to 'Miami', but my flight is going to 'Minneapolis'. Passengers are confused. Can you fix the typo?"
msel.expectedAction: Ops logs a ticket with IT. IT likely treats this as a minor display error/glitch.

msel.event: Ticket #4492 (Noise): Vending machines in Concourse B are spitting out soda cans randomly.
msel.expectedAction: IT ignores or deprioritizes (correctly). Ops calls maintenance.

msel.event: Ticket Update: "We checked the FIDS server. The data stream from the AODB is actually sending 'Miami'. It's not a display error; the source data changed."
msel.expectedAction: IT investigates the AODB logs. Ops assumes it's a one-off database error.

msel.event: Radio Call: "Ops, TSA Checkpoint. We have passengers scanning boarding passes for a HWK Air flight to Chicago, but the FIDS board in the lobby lists that flight as 'Cancelled'. They are arguing with my TSOs."
msel.expectedAction: Ops must verify flight status with HWK Air directly. Realize the data on screens contradicts reality.

msel.event: Tweet (@TravelGuy99): "NCIA is a joke! Boards say my flight is at Gate A1. I walked to A1 and it's empty. App says A12. Now I'm gonna miss my flight! #Fail"
msel.expectedAction: PIO monitors sentiment. Ops realizes the error is spreading to multiple flights.

msel.event: SCENARIO JUMP: It is now 10:00 AM. The errors are multiplying. 20% of flights on the big board show incorrect times or gates.
msel.expectedAction: Activate Section 13.6 (FIDS Failure). Ops should consider putting "Whiteboard Teams" on standby.

citations.headingPath: TIRP › Section 13 › 13.6 Scenario C: FIDS / BHS System Failure

msel.event: Radio Call (Red Herring): Fire alarm reported in the Long Term Parking Deck.
msel.expectedAction: Ops dispatches Fire to garage but keeps Police/Ops focused on the terminal issues.

msel.event: Audio/Visual Inject: The terminal PA system announces: "Attention passengers. Flight 666 to Purgatory is now boarding at all gates." FIDS screens show the same.
msel.expectedAction: CRITICAL DECISION POINT: Ops must silence the PA system immediately. IT must disconnect the PA server from the network.

citations.headingPath: TIRP › Section 1 › 1.4 Guidance Applicable for All Incident Plans › 1.4.5 Use of Communication Systems

msel.event: Facebook Post: Viral rumor claiming ISIS has taken over the control tower and planes are crashing.
msel.expectedAction: PIO must issue an immediate "Myth Busting" statement denying physical threats to aircraft.

msel.event: Phone Call: "Ops, Baggage Control here. The sortation logic is corrupted. The system is sending all bags for Concourse A (Skyline/HWK Air) to the 'Manual Encode' pier in the basement. The belt is jammed."
msel.expectedAction: Ops coordinates with Airlines to initiate manual baggage handling. Massive delays expected.

msel.event: Email Forward: Intern admits to clicking a phishing link ("Free Ironclads Tickets") on workstation OPS_INTERN_03.
msel.expectedAction: IT identifies "Patient Zero" and begins isolating that workstation to stop the attack vector.

msel.event: Face-to-Face: (Angry) "Our pilots are refusing to push back because their electronic flight bags are syncing with your airport data, and it's feeding them bad gate info. We are grounding all flights until you confirm your data is clean."
msel.expectedAction: Ops must declare an official Incident. Establish Unified Command.

msel.event: Technical Update: "We have found unauthorized admin access in the AODB SQL database. Someone is running a script (random_gate_generator.ps1) that randomizes gate assignments."
msel.expectedAction: DECISION POINT: Ops must authorize a total shutdown of FIDS. The terminal screens go black.

msel.event: Visual Inject: Show a photo of a crowded terminal with blank screens. Passengers are crowding around airline counters demanding info. Noise levels are high.
msel.expectedAction: Ops deploys staff with megaphones and whiteboards (Section 13.7 Checklist). PIO puts out "Go to your airline app" messaging.

citations.headingPath: TIRP › Section 1 › 1.4 Guidance Applicable for All Incident Plans › 1.4.5 Use of Communication Systems

msel.event: Phone Call: TSA screening is stopping because boarding pass data doesn't match the system. Lines are backing up dangerously.
msel.expectedAction: Ops/LEO must manage the crowd crush at the checkpoint. Ops may ask TSA to move to "manual ID check" mode.

msel.event: Radio Call: "Crowd crush situation at Gate C4. Two flights were directed there by the old screen data. Passengers are fighting over seats."
msel.expectedAction: Gate C4 does not exist: it is the bad data's gate (a planted tell). Ops finds where the two crowds actually are (the B10 hold room at the end of Concourse B) and directs Police there. Priority shifts to crowd control and safety over flight operations.

citations.documentTitle: Terminal Incident Response Plan
citations.headingPath: TIRP › Section 4: Repopulation

msel.event: Phone Call: "Channel 5 News here. Going live in 15 minutes. We are reporting this is 'Cyber Terror'. Comment now or we run with it."
msel.expectedAction: PIO must issue a holding statement that calms the public without confirming details they don't have yet.

msel.event: Technical Update: "We have isolated the compromised server and restored the AODB from a backup taken at 04:00 AM. We believe the data is clean."
msel.expectedAction: IT requests permission to bring FIDS back online.

msel.event: Threat: "If you turn those screens on and they show bad info again, I am pulling my staff. I need a guarantee."
msel.expectedAction: Ops hesitates. Asks IT for a verification plan.

msel.event: Operational Query: "Before we turn the screens on, how do we know the script isn't still hidden?"
msel.expectedAction: IT and Ops devise a testing plan (e.g., turn on one single screen at a remote gate to verify).

msel.event: Error Message: "Backup Tape Library Not Mounted." Restoration hits a snag.
msel.expectedAction: IT must troubleshoot or find an alternate backup source. Delaying recovery.

msel.event: Coordination: "We need to manually verify every flight in the system before you publish it."
msel.expectedAction: A tedious "data reconciliation" process begins between Airport Ops and Airlines.

msel.event: ENDEX (End Exercise). The screens are successfully restored.
msel.expectedAction: Move to Hot Wash / Debrief.

metrics.name: Operational Coordination
metrics.fail: Ops ignored IT and kept bad data on screens, causing chaos.
metrics.pass: Ops consulted IT but delayed the "Go Dark" decision until injects forced it.
metrics.excellence: Ops proactively established a "Manual Operations Plan" (whiteboards) before shutting down the screens.

metrics.name: Technical Competence
metrics.fail: IT rebooted the compromised server immediately (destroying evidence).
metrics.pass: IT identified the "UPDATE" command in the logs but didn't find the source IP.
metrics.excellence: IT identified the SQL Injection, isolated the specific workstation (192.168.1.55), and preserved logs for the FBI.

metrics.name: Public Communication
metrics.fail: PIO stayed silent or confirmed "Terrorism" without evidence.
metrics.excellence: PIO actively countered misinformation (the "ISIS" rumor) with calm, factual updates across multiple channels.

metrics.name: Use of Doctrine
metrics.fail: Students "winged it" and never opened the AEP/TIRP/ASP.
metrics.pass: Students referenced the plans but struggled to find sections.
metrics.excellence: Students cited specific sections (e.g., "Per TIRP Section 13.6, we are activating manual backups").

objectiveCapabilities.why: The objective requires timely, coordinated, and reliable messaging to the public and media during a cyber incident, which directly aligns with Public Information and Warning, ensuring consistent and actionable information is delivered via all channels.

The objective involves integrating IT, Operations, and Public Information roles into a unified response structure, which is the core function of Operational Coordination to ensure all stakeholders act in concert.
The objective centers on making life-safety and operational decisions under uncertainty, requiring continuous assessment of threat status, system behavior, and impact—key to Situational Assessment.

High-consequence decisions must be made in coordination across technical and operational leadership; this objective depends on a unified command structure to synchronize decisions, which is the purpose of Operational Coordination.

The objective directly tests the ability to identify a cyberattack vector (SQL injection, compromised credential) from technical logs, which is the core function of Cybersecurity in protecting and restoring systems.

The root cause involves unauthorized access to the AODB via credential compromise, which falls under Access Control and Identity Verification, as it relates to protecting system integrity and preventing unauthorized access.

hotwash.methodDescription: Ask the room to identify three things that went well and three things that broke/failed.

questions.text: At what point did you stop trusting the screens? Why did it take so long?
Ops, did you understand what IT was saying? IT, did you understand what Ops needed?
How did you handle the revelation that the attack came from an intern's computer? Did you treat it as a crime scene or a tech support ticket?

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment where players are encouraged to explore decisions without fear of real-world consequences.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented, with no external interference or changes to the injects.
Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures as documented in the TIRP, AEP, and related annexes.
All injects are authentic and reflect real-time developments as perceived by the players in the room.
The SimCell manages all external actors (e.g., law enforcement, cyber task force, vendors) and system behavior not directly controlled by the players.
Time advances only as specified in the injects, with no continuity assumed between modules beyond what is explicitly stated.
artificialities: Time jumps between modules are simulated; the exercise progresses in discrete 60-minute phases with no in-module time progression.
The SimCell plays all roles not in the room, including law enforcement, cyber task force, and external vendor contacts.
System names (e.g., AODB, FIDS, BHS) are used as in the plans but are not physically accessed or modified by players.
Injects are delivered via paper, screen, or audio-visual means and reflect only what is visible to the players in the room.
The root cause (SQL injection via compromised credential) is not revealed until Phase 4, and players must infer it from logs and behavior.

modules.narrativeMd: It is 09:00. The terminal is bustling with passengers due to a holiday weekend. Weather is clear, and operations are running normally. The FIDS displays show accurate flight information, and airport staff are managing routine operations. At 09:15, an airline representative calls Ops to report a display error on a gate screen: a flight to Minneapolis is listed as going to Miami. At 09:20, a helpdesk ticket reports that vending machines in Concourse B are dispensing drinks unexpectedly. At 09:30, IT confirms that the source data from the AODB is actually sending 'Miami' as the destination, not a display glitch. At 09:45, TSA reports a discrepancy: passengers are scanning boarding passes for a flight to Chicago, but the FIDS shows it as 'Cancelled'. At 09:55, a viral social media post from @TravelGuy99 mocks the airport's reliability, claiming flight information is inconsistent across screens and apps.
keyIssues: Is this a display glitch or a systemic data issue? When should an incident be declared?
How to respond to conflicting reports from multiple sources (airline, TSA, social media) without confirmation from IT?
Should the IT Department be notified immediately, or can it be handled via helpdesk ticketing?
How to prevent premature public messaging that could worsen confusion or panic?
How to balance technical verification against operational urgency when passenger flow is already affected.

modules.narrativeMd: It is now 10:00. The situation has escalated rapidly. The FIDS now shows 20% of flights with incorrect times or gates. At 10:00, a PA announcement falsely declares that Flight 666 to Purgatory is boarding at all gates. The FIDS screens mirror the message, causing panic. At 10:10, a fire alarm is reported in the Long Term Parking Deck—this is a red herring, but it adds to the confusion. At 10:15, a viral Facebook post claims that ISIS has taken over the control tower and planes are crashing. At 10:30, the BHS Control reports that the sortation logic is corrupted and all bags for Skyline and HWK Air are being sent to the manual encode pier, jamming the belt. At 10:40, IT confirms that an intern clicked a phishing link on workstation OPS_INTERN_03. At 10:45, an airline representative confronts Ops in person, stating that pilots are refusing to push back because their EFBs are syncing with corrupted data. The airport is no longer operating as normal.
keyIssues: How to determine if the FIDS, BHS, and EFB systems are compromised or independently failing?
When to declare a full cyber incident and activate the EOC under AEP Section 3.5?
How to manage a growing public panic when media is already reporting 'cyber terror'?
How to ensure that IT’s technical findings are trusted by operations and airlines?
How to prevent operational paralysis when multiple systems fail simultaneously and evidence is incomplete.

modules.narrativeMd: It is now 11:00. The terminal is in manual mode. The FIDS screens are blank. The PA system has been silenced. At 11:00, IT confirms that the compromised server has been isolated and the AODB has been restored from a backup taken at 04:00 AM. However, at 11:15, a photo of the terminal is shown: crowds are gathering around airline counters, passengers are shouting, and the noise level is high. At 11:20, TSA reports that screening is halting because boarding pass data no longer matches the system. At 11:30, a radio call from security reports a crowd crush at Gate C4, where two flights were directed by old data. The airport is now operating under manual procedures. Whiteboards, paper manifests, and bullhorns are being used to relay information. The airport must manage passenger flow and maintain order without digital tools.
keyIssues: How to implement manual/analog procedures across all departments when digital systems are down?
How to ensure consistency and accuracy in manual data entry across multiple teams?
How to manage passenger flow and prevent physical incidents like crowd crushes when information is not centralized?
How to maintain trust with airlines when manual verification is required for every flight?
How to prevent confusion when manual procedures are not yet standardized across teams.

modules.narrativeMd: It is now 12:00. The airport is preparing to restore the FIDS and other systems. At 12:00, IT confirms that the AODB has been restored from a backup taken at 04:00 AM. However, at 12:10, a server error message appears: 'Backup Tape Library Not Mounted.' The restoration process is blocked. At 12:15, an airline representative demands a guarantee that the data is clean before any screens are turned on. At 12:20, IT confirms that the backup tape is not mounted, so the system cannot be restored from that point. At 12:30, airlines demand manual verification of every flight in the system before any data is published. The airport must now decide whether to trust the restored data, and how to verify it without a functioning network.
keyIssues: How to verify data integrity when the backup is not mounted and no clean restore is possible?
How to decide whether to go 'dark' again or proceed with a potentially compromised system?
How to balance the need for speed in restoring operations with the need for verification?
How to rebuild public trust when the system has been restored from an incomplete backup?
How to manage the risk of a second failure if the system is reactivated without full verification.
